To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce a novel hierarchical crossmodal reinforcement learning architecture that can learn from multiple sensory inputs; (2) the architecture can learn from a variety of modalities, such as vision and sound; and (3) the architecture can accelerate the learning of new skills by leveraging the learned latent features from previously learned tasks

(1) we introduce CASL, a novel architecture that integrates the A2OC architecture with attention, (2) we demonstrate that CASL is able to transfer knowledge from a single sensory modality to another, and (3) we demonstrate CASL can learn to attend to the most relevant features in an image and audio input to improve performance in a single sensory mod-ality.
1. We introduce CASL, a crossmodal attentive skill learner, that can learn to use multiple sensory inputs to improve performance.
